Breaking changes are called out.
Some changes break data that already exists. Make
‘s
a string at the same version, and the app versions already
installed keep sending an integer, which a collector validating against the new document rejects.
Records the app stored at that version no longer decode, and its store drops them. While the
committed plan still has the old shape, the check reports changes like these as breaking, names the
event and the property, and says to undo the change or raise the event’s version. “Checking the
plan” below shows how to keep CI failing on them after the plan is exported again.
Privacy review reads the same files.
Each event’s consent category and each
property are in its document. A change to either fails the check until the plan is exported again,
so it shows up in the pull request as well.
Services can validate against it.
TraffluentCollector loads the exported directory and checks
each record’s properties against its event’s document. It rejects a record that doesn’t match,
naming the property and the rule it broke, and its dashboards offer the plan’s events and their
typed properties. Any JSON Schema 2020-12 validator can check payloads against the same documents.
A destination that redacts

requires a
property, so the redacted record still validates.

metadata.title: Exporting and Checking a Tracking Plan

abstract.text: Stamp every event with its session and with the app, device, system, locale and network it was tracked on.
Keep a seeded fraction of the events a tracker tracks, event by event or a whole session at once.
Export every event an app tracks as JSON Schema that people and services outside the app can read, and check each change against the plan committed before it.
Typed analytics events for Swift, delivered in batches to any number of destinations.
Send events to an analytics vendor Traffluent doesn’t cover yet, from a module of your own, with the same rules as the destinations it ships.
Fail a Swift Testing test when an app’s events no longer match its committed tracking plan, so every change to an event comes with a change to the plan.
Keep each record on disk until it is delivered, so a record the app tracked survives the process ending.
Track screen views, control activations and the app’s lifecycle without a call at each place they happen.
Derive an event’s conformances and schema from its declaration with
, and constrain which values its properties may hold.
Deliver an event only once the user grants the purpose it is collected for.
